messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: PyStan Issues on OS X?
parts:
I’m having a hell of a time trying to install PyStan 2.11.0 on OS X 10.9.

I can clone stan-dev/pystan and compile from source, which seems
to end successfully with

running install_lib
copying build/lib.macosx-10.9-intel-2.7/pystan/__init__.py -> /Library/Python/2.7/site-packages/pystan

But then if I try to import in that directory I get the error

>>> import pystan
Traceback (most recent call last):
File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
File "pystan/__init__.py", line 9, in <module>
from pystan.api import stanc, stan
File "pystan/api.py", line 12, in <module>
import pystan._api # stanc wrapper
ImportError: No module named _api

and if I try to import from another directory I get

>>> import pystan
Traceback (most recent call last):
File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
ImportError: No module named pystan

If I try to install via pip I get weird errors like

error: can't copy 'pystan/_api.c': doesn't exist or not a regular file

----------------------------------------
Cleaning up...
Command /usr/bin/python -c "import setuptools, tokenize;__file__='/private/tmp/pip_build_root/pystan/setup.py';exec(compile(getattr(tokenize, 'open', open)(__file__).read().replace('\r\n', '\n'), __file__, 'exec'))" install --record /tmp/pip-QJwK86-record/install-record.txt --single-version-externally-managed --compile failed with error code 1 in /private/tmp/pip_build_root/pystan
Storing debug log for failure in /Users/Betancourt/Library/Logs/pip.log

Anyone having more success?

I’m trying to install PyStan as I have a colleague who is seeing the 2.10 bug
persist in the PyStan 2.11 installion, which would be bad news all around,
but I can’t verify because I can’t even get it installed. :-(

messages.author: ff89d4c4917094ad
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] PyStan Issues on OS X?
parts:
This is a directory name gotcha. If there's a `pystan` directory in the
current working directory Python will try to import stuff from there
when you type `import pystan`. You just need to change your directory
(e.g., 'cd /tmp') and things will work. Then it will import pystan from,
as you can see below, `/Library/Python/2.7/site-packages/pystan` where
all the compiled binaries went (including, _api.so, the source of the
import error)

There is a note about this in the documentation.

If you want to have Python install stuff directly into the current
working checkout you can do this: python setup.py build_ext --inplace
